query: Consider the following context: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys (HEAs) are promising candidates for low-dimensional magnetocaloric applications. In that context, which method can be used for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A machine-learning-driven approach to systematically tune high-entropy alloy microstructure through thermomechanical process parameters (such as annealing temperature, cooling rate, and deformation extent) can significantly adjust the magnetocaloric response of non-equiatomic HEAs, compared to unoptimized conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloy sample with baseline composition and as-cast microstructure suitable for magnetocaloric applications
generation.intervention: Implement a machine-learning-based high-throughput optimization scheme that systematically dictates thermomechanical processing (e.g., annealing temperature, cooling rate, forming steps).
generation.conditions: Vary annealing temperatures between 800–1200 K, cooling rates from 1–50 K/s, and up to 50% cold working prior to heat treatment, guided by iterative machine learning predictions of processing–structure–property relationships.
generation.structural_mediator: Subtle changes in phase fractions, domain structure, short-range ordering, and morphological evolution in the non-equiatomic HEA
generation.mechanism: Data-driven process selection identifies correlations between local microstructural evolution, magnetic transition temperature, and magnetocaloric performance, enabling systematic tuning of processing pathways to enhance magnetic entropy change near operating temperatures.
generation.predicted_outcome: Alloys processed under machine-learning-optimized conditions will exhibit measurable enhancement of magnetic hysteresis and magnetocaloric performance, surpassing that of conventional baseline treatments by around 10–20%.
generation.baseline: Undifferentiated as-cast non-equiatomic HEA with conventional heat treatment not guided by data-driven strategies
generation.boundary: Effectiveness restricted to non-equiatomic alloys that remain in single- or fine-scale multi-phase regimes. Large composition changes beyond the initial specified range are not covered by this method.
generation.uncertainty: Lack of sufficiently comprehensive input data could limit model accuracy. Extrapolation to new, untested composition or processing regimes requires extra validation.

falsification_experiment.design: Produce a set of non-equiatomic HEA samples processed at varying hours and temperatures, with and without machine-learning-derived schedules. Compare magnetization, phase distribution, and magnetocaloric performance for each sample.
measurements: X-ray diffraction and SEM-based phase analysis to identify microstructural changes
VSM (vibrating sample magnetometry) or SQUID measurements of magnetization vs. temperature
Direct or indirect measurement of magnetocaloric effect (entropy change) near target operating temperatures
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples processed under the optimized, data-driven schedules do not show improved magnetocaloric performance (by at least the expected level of ~10–20%) over conventional treatments, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
The concept of HEAs provides us an unprecedented degree of freedom in the design of advanced alloys with promising properties. For the rapid exploration of the vast compositional space and investigation of the composition and temperature effects on the microstructure, advanced HEA-design strategies and efficient tools are necessary. At present, a few advanced HEA-design strategies were reported by combining the physicochemical criteria, CALPHAD, data mining, and multi-objective optimization algorithm [21] , [22] , [35] – [37] , demonstrating that the CALPHAD method has played an important role in the design of advanced HEAs. There are two essential requirements to carry out calculations, using the CALPHAD method: computational software and database.

The computational software could significantly affect the efficiency of HTC since massive calculations are carried out. In the example of the Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti quinary system, it takes only a few hours on a desktop computer to finish the HTCs (~ 3 × 10 3 ) within the composition range of 5–50 at.% for each element and finally screen out eight potential alloys. decision.trend: In the only earlier paper dealing with magnetically active high-entropy alloys (FeCoNiTi), researchers identified multiple ferromagnetic transitions and found that intricate phase formation and magnetocrystalline anisotropy strongly affect coercivity and saturation magnetization. Although the fundamental magnetism was characterized, the systematic optimization of magnetocaloric performance—particularly in non-equiatomic compositions—remains unexplored. The key insight is that subtle changes in phase assemblies and short-range ordering can strongly influence magnetic transitions, yet established studies have focused on single-composition or equiatomic alloys without a broad, systematic survey of possible microstructures and process conditions.
decision.unsolved: How to leverage thermomechanical pathways (rather than simply adding new elements) to steer microstructure and magnetic-domain architectures for enhanced magnetocaloric effects, especially in low-dimensional non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys, remains unresolved. A high-throughput, rigorous method to navigate the large parameter space of compositions, annealing schedules, and microstructural states is still needed.
decision.lever: A machine-learning-driven approach to map the influence of processing variables (e.g., annealing profiles, deformation paths, or cooling rates) on the resulting magnetic transitions and magnetocaloric response, using performance-driven models trained on available HEA data to guide targeted small-scale experiments.
decision.why: Because existing work has established the critical role of subtle structural and magnetic changes in shaping magnetocaloric properties, a data-driven strategy can efficiently explore the vast parameter space of non-equiatomic HEAs without defaulting to composition changes. By correlating process conditions, resulting microstructures, and magnetocaloric performance, machine learning can rapidly identify promising processing paths for tuning the magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
